A1.justification: Both readable, complete 16-page PDFs describe the same RecPO study. The methods, experiments, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F can be matched despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: V1 reports original experiments on five recommendation datasets, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, behavioral probes, and Appendix F's sensitivity analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experimental results in Tables 1–2 and Figures 2, 4, and 6, including the appendix analysis.

M1.justification: The complete-history prompts, rating signals, temporal utility, adaptive ratio margin, and multi-negative optimization objective remain unchanged. V2's preference-intensity and temporal-context terminology describes existing components.

E1.justification: Both versions use MovieLens-1M, Amazon-Books, BeerAdvocate, Steam, and LastFM for the same recommendation task and behavioral probes. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same traditional and LLM-based comparators, and Figure 4 retains SFT and S-DPO. GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 were already excluded in v1; revising the exclusion explanation does not change evaluated comparator membership.

E3.justification: The data splits, candidate construction, positive-item selection, evaluation metrics, model sizes, optimization settings, and testing procedures are retained. No new evaluation design is introduced; the hardware-reporting revision is addressed under D1.

E4.justification: The four input configurations in Figure 2, margin-function ablation in Table 2, behavioral and history-length probes in Figure 4, and margin sensitivity in Figure 6 are unchanged. V2's controlled-ablation framing introduces no additional tests.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The descriptive history-length variance comparison, 8.7% versus 17.8%, is retained without a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–2 and empirical plots in Figures 2, 4, and 6 match. For example, LLaMA3-8B RecPO's MovieLens and Amazon-Books HR@1 remain 0.3451 and 0.5802. No experimental result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, utility and margin definitions, and Appendix B's preference-distribution derivation are unchanged. Appendix A receives a grammatical correction without changing its formal definitions.

C1.justification: V1 primarily contributes a RecPO framework for human-like preference profiling. V2 recasts the central contribution as hypothesis-driven empirical identification of preference intensity and temporal context, claiming controlled ablations establish these factors and presenting RecPO as their operationalization. This substantially redefines the claimed contribution in the introduction and conclusion, although the abstract is largely retained.

C2.justification: V2 attributes individual behavioral benefits more explicitly to the two factors and broadens Table 2's interpretation from the utility of margin-aware optimization to improvement through any margin formulation. The baseline-exclusion rationale changes from model-scale fairness to training access. The limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: V1 consistently reports up to eight A6000 GPUs with 48 GB. V2 Section 5.1 instead reports eight A100 GPUs with 80 GiB, while Appendix E.3 retains the A6000 description, leaving the actual hardware unresolved. Software versions, hyperparameters, and access links are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Bai et al. (2023) for Qwen and removes several general recommendation references and the excluded-model citations. Its main-text positioning emphasizes investigating overlooked factors instead of the specific margin-construction distinction from ODPO. The detailed related-work discussion in Appendix D is retained.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the title, introduction, proof-of-concept discussion, and conclusion, and reorganizes the experimental narrative around research questions. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, and numerous headings and contribution statements are rewritten.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 are visually revised; Figure 3 changes from a DPO/RecPO schematic to binary/enriched preference with revised graphics and labels. Existing figures and tables move with text reflow, including Figure 6 moving to page 15. Empirical plot designs and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a clearer narrative, but its new claim that controlled ablations identify both factors exceeds the retained evidence: Figure 2 varies history completeness and ratings, while Table 2 varies margin forms; neither independently isolates temporal context. V2 also introduces conflicting hardware descriptions between Section 5.1 and Appendix E.3. With the method and empirical support unchanged, these limited losses in evidential precision and reproducibility outweigh the editorial gains.
